For years, there have been rumours that Apple is developing a brand-new all-glass iPhone model to celebrate the 20th anniversary of the iPhone next year. However, an analyst at Jefferies believes the device will no longer be moving forward.

A Wall Street analyst says the major redesign of the iPhone to mark the 20th anniversary has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies has downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee arguing that the major revamp of the 20th-anniversary iPhone is likely off the table — a key reason behind the downgrade.

At the heart of the downgrade is the view that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been dead in the water. Although reports dating back to 2025 indicated the project was in development, with rumours of a launch as early as 2027, Apple has never responded to such speculation. That said, the company did quietly file a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered an all-glass iPhone a reasonable idea, but Lee now believes development has stalled. The analyst noted that supply-chain checks indicate the project was scrapped due to low yield rates. Lee said that, with memory costs continuing to rise, this represents "a major setback for driving high-end iPhone sales." If the device had launched in September 2027 as planned to mark the iPhone's 20th anniversary, its blended retail price was expected to reach US$2,060 — higher than the average selling price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further lifting average selling prices and margins." He argued that, with memory prices climbing, this is a crucial defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed to Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro as additional reasons for the downgrade.

From Lee's report, it's impossible to tell whether he believes the entire redesign project has been shelved, or only certain design elements have been dropped.

Top comment posted by Currentinterest

These analysts have been wrong about Apple's future plans many times before. The "all-glass" label probably never accurately reflected what Apple really wanted to deliver. Whatever the final specs turn out to be, this 20th-anniversary phone will be distinctive and have people clamouring for it.

For example, there has been speculation that Apple may not be able to completely eliminate the Dynamic Island cutout next year. That would make a truly "all-glass" display impossible. However, a rumoured four-sided curved design could still debut first.

In any case, if the redesign of Apple's 20th-anniversary iPhone really has been cancelled, other credible sources are likely to confirm it in the short term.
